evidence: Cic. Sen. 33: at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs
Ter. Haut. 342: in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē ut dormiās
terms.comment: Either one, it does not matter which.

phrases.latin: ita magnae utrimque cōpiae, ita parātae ad dēpugnandum esse dīcuntur, ut, utercumque vīcerit, nōn sit mīrum futūrum
phrases.english: the forces on both sides are said to be so large and so ready to fight it out that, whichever of them wins, it will be no surprise

phrases.latin: At minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs.
phrases.english: But I have less strength than either of you.

phrases.latin: in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē ut dormiās
phrases.english: so that you can sleep soundly on whichever ear you like

sources: Lewis & Short: utercumque · Lewis & Short: utervis · Lewis & Short: quicumque
Cicero (Letters to Friends, De senectute), Terence and Caesar checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
